$comment: Registry for issue #834's CI-enforced mutation gate.
SCHEMA v2 (issue #854): this file used to hold every mutant as one entry in a
'mutants' array. That made it a guaranteed conflict generator -- every security-fix
PR appends an entry at the same insertion point, and multiple PRs landing the same
day (#848/#849/#850, 2026-07-28) collided on that exact spot even though nothing
else about any of them conflicted. As of v2, this file holds ONLY the schema version
and this shared guidance comment. Every mutant is its own file under
test/mutants/entries/<id>.json, containing exactly the object that used to be one
element of the 'mutants' array. The file's basename (without .json) MUST equal the
entry's own 'id' field -- test/mutants/run_mutant.py enforces this and refuses to
load a mismatched file. Two concurrent PRs registering two different mutants now
add two different files and cannot conflict with each other.
test/mutants/run_mutant.py and .github/workflows/mutation-gate.yml discover mutants
by globbing test/mutants/entries/*.json, not by reading an array from this file. Both
fail loudly (non-zero exit) if the glob finds nothing, or if any discovered file is
missing an 'id' -- a directory listing being empty must never be mistaken for 'no
mutants configured, nothing to do, pass'.
Each entry describes ONE mutant: a small, reviewable patch against exactly one
production file, plus the test filter that MUST turn red when the patch is applied
(the 'exploit'/detection filter) and the test filter that MUST stay green (the
positive control, proving the harness itself still works and the mutation did not
have broader collateral effects than declared).
kind:
security  - a real mutant against production security-fix code. Run by the main
'mutants' job in .github/workflows/mutation-gate.yml. A non-KILLED
verdict on ANY security-kind entry is ALWAYS a gate failure -- there is
no per-entry override. That is intentional: this registry is a forcing
function, not a place to declare a known-broken test 'expected' and move
on (that is precisely the loophole issue #834 exists to close).
selftest  - a meta-fixture used only to test the runner (run_mutant.py) itself, e.g.
to prove a non-compiling patch is reported as an invalid mutant and never
as a pass. Run by the separate 'meta-selftest' job, invoked with
--expect-verdict so the *runner's own correctness* is what is asserted,
not any real security property. selftest entries are never mixed into the
main gate's pass/fail decision.
red_expected_assertion_patterns maps each red_tests[] fully-qualified test name to a
regex that MUST match that test's MSTest failure message for the kill to count. This is
what stops rule-of-thumb 'non-zero exit = detected': a test that goes red with an
unrelated NullReferenceException or a fixture crash does not match and is reported as
UNEXPECTED_RED (gate failure), not KILLED.
